summary:
TERRA-SCAN is our attempt to make satellite imagery easier to understand and more useful in solving real-world environmental challenges. Inspired by NASA's Earth observation resources and the Dancing with the Stars challenge, we wanted to build a platform that does more than simply display satellite images. We wanted to help people understand what is happening on the ground and why those changes matter.

Satellite data contains an enormous amount of information about our planet, but accessing it, interpreting it, and turning it into something meaningful can be difficult, especially for people without a technical or scientific background.
The platform brings satellite imagery and Earth observation resources into one place, allowing users to explore different geographical regions, examine environmental changes, and understand patterns that might otherwise go unnoticed.
Our focus is on areas where understanding environmental changes can make a real difference, including river corridors, geological fault zones, land-use changes, and other regions of environmental interest.
What makes TERRA-SCAN meaningful to us is the idea behind it: satellite imagery should not be limited to researchers or people who know how to interpret scientific datasets. Students, environmental enthusiasts, researchers, and decision-makers should also be able to explore this information without facing a steep technical learning curve.
details:
TERRA-SCAN is an AI-assisted Earth observation platform developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our idea comes from a simple observation: satellites continuously collect enormous amounts of information about our planet, but making sense of that information is not always easy. Accessing satellite datasets, understanding different types of imagery, and identifying meaningful patterns often requires technical knowledge and specialised tools. We wanted to make this process simpler, more interactive, and accessible to a wider audience.

What does TERRA-SCAN do and how does it work?

TERRA-SCAN provides a platform where users can explore geographical regions and work with satellite imagery to better understand changes and patterns on Earth's surface. Instead of treating satellite images as standalone pictures, our approach focuses on helping users interpret the information they contain.

Users can explore areas of interest, upload satellite imagery where supported, and use the platform's analysis interface to examine geographical features. Our planned AI-assisted analysis engine is designed to identify relevant visual patterns and present observations in a more understandable format.

We are particularly interested in environmentally and geographically significant regions, including the Brahmaputra River corridor, the San Andreas Fault Zone, and other areas where studying changes in the Earth's surface can provide valuable insights.

The project also takes inspiration from NASA's Earth observation ecosystem and publicly available resources, helping connect users with the wider world of satellite data.

What benefits does it offer?

The biggest benefit of TERRA-SCAN is that it attempts to reduce the gap between collecting satellite data and understanding it.

  • Accessibility: Makes satellite imagery and its interpretation more approachable for students, researchers, and people without specialised technical knowledge.
  • Simplified analysis: Aims to reduce the complexity involved in exploring and interpreting geographical imagery.
  • Environmental awareness: Encourages users to observe and understand changes in rivers, landscapes, geological regions, and other important environments.
  • Centralised experience: Brings exploration, imagery analysis, and understandable insights together in one platform.
  • Educational value: Can serve as a learning and exploration tool for people interested in geography, Earth science, environmental studies, and remote sensing.

What is the intended impact?

Our long-term vision is to make Earth observation useful beyond the scientific community. We believe that understanding our planet should not require everyone to become a remote-sensing expert.

TERRA-SCAN aims to support environmental education, geographical research, and better awareness of changes occurring across different parts of the world. In the future, the platform could also assist researchers and organisations in identifying areas that deserve closer investigation.

We see potential applications in studying river systems, monitoring landscape changes, understanding geological features, and supporting environmental research. However, our intention is to complement scientific investigation rather than replace professional assessment or official monitoring systems.

Tools and technologies used

We chose technologies that would allow us to develop a modular, interactive, and scalable web platform.

  • Frontend: React.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js.
  • AI/ML: Python, with libraries and computer vision frameworks such as PyTorch, YOLO, and OpenCV for image-processing and analysis capabilities.
  • Geospatial visualisation: Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.
  • Database: PostgreSQL and Supabase.
  • External resources: NASA Earthdata and other publicly available Earth observation datasets and resources.
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code, GitHub, GitHub Desktop, and AI-assisted development tools.

The project is designed around a modular architecture so that additional datasets, analysis models, and features can be integrated as development progresses.

What makes TERRA-SCAN creative?

We did not want to build another website that simply displays satellite images on a map. Our creative approach was to focus on the experience of understanding those images.

We are combining geographical exploration, AI-assisted image analysis, and interactive visualisation to make Earth observation feel less like working with complicated scientific software and more like exploring our planet through meaningful information.

We also wanted the platform to connect scientific data with real-world locations. Exploring a river corridor or a geological fault zone should help users understand why that particular region is important, what they can observe there, and what further questions they might investigate.

What factors did our team consider?

While developing TERRA-SCAN, we considered several important factors:

  1. Data accessibility: We wanted to build around publicly available and credible Earth observation resources rather than depend entirely on closed datasets.
  2. Usability: The interface needed to be understandable even for first-time users with limited knowledge of satellite imagery.
  3. Accuracy and reliability: AI-generated observations should not be presented as scientifically verified conclusions without appropriate validation.
  4. Scalability: The architecture should allow new geographical regions, datasets, and analysis models to be added in the future.
  5. Performance: We considered the computational requirements of image processing and aimed for a modular approach that could work without depending entirely on expensive computing resources.
  6. Real-world relevance: We prioritised use cases where satellite imagery could help people better understand environmental and geographical changes.

Our Vision

TERRA-SCAN is a step towards making satellite intelligence more understandable and accessible. We started with the belief that the information collected from space has enormous value, but that value increases when more people can interpret and use it.

Through this project, we hope to bring people a little closer to understanding our planet, one satellite image at a time.
